blogs.title: Fair Use at the Forefront: How the Second Circuit’s Santos v. Kimmel Ruling Expands the Transformative‑Use Threshold
blogs.description: This post dissects the court’s emphasis on the *reasonable observer* test for transformative use, noting the shift from subjective intent to objective evaluation. It examines how the decision extends fair‑use preemption into commentary‑driven audiences and what this means for creators of derivative content on streaming platforms.

blogs.title: Contractual Pitfalls in the Digital Age: Why Non‑Contracting Third Parties Can’t Hop on a Platform’s Terms of Service
blogs.description: Focusing on the state‑law breach‑of‑contract arguments, this analysis explores the strong presumption against extending the terms of service to non‑signatories, the role of third‑party beneficiary doctrine under Illinois and New‑York law, and the practical implications for influencers, content‑sharing services, and their audiences.

blogs.title: Fraudulent Inducement Without Loss: The New York Standard and the Limits of Allegations in Platform‑Related Disputes
blogs.description: This article reviews the court’s application of the New York “out‑of‑pocket loss” requirement for fraud, arguing that the Santos case clarifies what constitutes a recoverable loss in platform‑based contractual claims. It also considers how this standard might affect future litigations involving online marketplaces and digital contracts.

blogs.title: Preemption, Fair Use, and State‑Law Claims: Why the Second Circuit Kept the Copyright Act King
blogs.description: A comprehensive examination of the court’s refusal to consider a preemption defense, the interplay between federal copyright protection and state‑law contractual claims, and the broader doctrinal trend toward upholding copyright over state‑law remedies in the face of commercial disputes.
